messages.subject: qtl analysis on RIL, troubles using risib
messages.subject_clean: qtl analysis on RIL, troubles using risib
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am a newbie in QTL and I have some troubles to analyze my data.  I
am trying to run rqtl for my Drosophila data. I was using "risib" that
I think would fit  for my recombinant lines (3 generations  of
recombination and  6 generations of full sibmating)?

library(qtl)
read.cross("csv",dir=".",file="data.csv")->myx
summary(myx)
class(myx)[1]<-"risib"
summary(myx)

For the first summary everything looks fine (even if the type cross is
F2 intercross),  I have the percentage for each genotype in letters:
Genotypes (%):      AA:37.3  AB:22.4  BB:40.3  not BB:0  not AA:0
But after changing the cross type into risib, the summary is weird:

Warning message:
In summary.cross(sxl2) : Invalid genotypes.
    Observed genotypes: 3 1 2 NA

and for all individuals the genotypes are transformed into numbers.

Is there a better way to do this?

Thanks for your help,

Audrey

messages.subject: Re: qtl analysis on RIL, troubles using risib
messages.subject_clean: qtl analysis on RIL, troubles using risib
messages.body_plain:
Three generations of random mating followed by six generations of full
sib mating doesn't really make
recombinant inbred lines.

Recombinant inbred lines would be homozygous AA or BB at any locus,
and so converting the cross
to risib, there is confusion about all of those heterozygous
genotypes.

This is something between advanced intercross lines and recombinant
inbred lines.  R/qtl can't really
handle this properly.  The best you can do is analyze it as an
intercross.

karl
--------
Karl Broman
kbr...@gmail.com

messages.subject: RI data format
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,
I am a newbie to QTL (and R/qtl). We have some RI data we would like
to analyse with R/qtl. What is the most suitable format for the
phenotype data? each strain was tested with 20-30 different
individuals.  Is there a way to feed the individual score (e.g.
replicate the same ID with the same genotype information several
times)?

I have noticed that the bristle3 dataset that comes with the qtl
library provides the phenotype information as mean and SD for each
RIL. However, when I use the command  summary(bristle3) there are seem
to be 9 phenotypes (while looking at the file made by write.cross
shows that  there are only 4 phenotypes, two columns for each which
include mean and SD). Is there a way to provide the phenotypic mean
and SD for each RIL? what is the best format to do that?

Many thanks in advance, any tip or advice will be much appreciated,
Eran

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] RI data format
messages.body_plain:
Analysis of recombinant inbred lines isn't very well developed in R/qtl.
We can only work with a single phenotype per line, such as the average.

I recommend using the "csv" or "csvr" formats.  You'll need to read the
data in as if they were from a backcross, and then change the cross type
to "risib" (or "riself"). See item #9 in the FAQ, http://www.rqtl.org/
faq/

karl
-----------
Karl Broman
kbr...@biostat.wisc.edu
http://www.biostat.wisc.edu/~kbroman
